newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-TOUGH BUDGET DISCIPLINE UNSUSTAINABLE - IMF.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-TOUGH BUDGET DISCIPLINE UNSUSTAINABLE - IMF.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) does not believe that the Latvian government can continue keeping such a tight grip on public finances as it is currently.
"This degree of expenditure restraint is not sustainable in the long term", IMF representative Dimitri Demekas told Reuters in an interview.
The IMF says the government needs to carry out structural reforms to be able to lift state revenue, enabling itself to increase expenditure.

"That is important, because it is all right to have a balanced budget, but when the only way to achieve it is by keeping spending and wages very low, which is how they have been doing it, it cannot go on forever", he said.
There is scope for the Latvian government to increase tax revenue, the IMF believes. "There is no need to raise taxes, just to collect the taxes owed," said Demekas.
Early signs indicate that Latvia is making progress in this area. "In the last few months of 1996 there is now evidence that tax administration has actually started improving.", said Demekas.
Land reform is another important area for the government, according to the IMF. Clear titles to land would facilitate banks giving credit for investment.
"As it is now, it is virtually impossible to have land as collateral for bank credit," Demekas pointed out.
